main_body: Anvil drawn in side profile: a wide grey face with a horn on the left, a dark waist, and a lighter base. A glowing orange and red piece sits on top.
top_band: Light grey band at rows 5-6 (the anvil face, with the horn to the left), then a mid-grey gradient at rows 7-8. It is only 2-3 rows and reads as the profile of the slab, not a surface seen from above.
evidence: Reading down the middle column: orange/red hot piece at rows 2-4, a thin light-grey anvil face at rows 5-6, a mid-grey taper at rows 7-8, a dark waist at rows 9-11, a lighter base band at rows 12-13, and a dark foot at row 14. The face and base are drawn as profile silhouettes with no clear horizontal surface seen from above, and there is no distinct front-edge line or eave shadow. This matches the side-elevation chair in the guide, so it fails.

style.evidence: The anvil uses about 4 grey steps with a dark neutral blue-black outline and almost no texture. The waist and base are flat blocks of one tone. The stall and well references carry many more colours per tile, with grain and tile detail, so the candidate looks thinner and more sticker-like beside them.
